Generate adaptive priors based on data characteristics

Source: R/utils-priors.R
generate_adaptive_priors.Rd

Generate adaptive priors based on data characteristics

Usage

generate_adaptive_priors(
  data,
  structure,
  model_type = "gaussian",
  outcome_var = structure$outcome_var %||% "outcome",
  exposure = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing the outcome and grouping variables.

structure

A list describing the hierarchical structure (from detect_hierarchical_structure).

model_type

Character string specifying the model family. Any brms family name is accepted and resolved by its default brms link: identity-link families use a response-scale intercept, log-link families ("poisson", "negbinomial", "Gamma", "weibull", "exponential", hurdle and zero-inflated count families, ...) and "lognormal" a log-scale intercept, and logit-type links ("bernoulli", "beta", "cumulative", ...) a link-scale intercept centered on 0.

outcome_var

Outcome column; defaults to structure$outcome_var, then "outcome".

exposure

Optional exposure column of a count model with an offset(log(<exposure>)) term (see add_exposure_offset()); the log-link intercept is then centered on the log of total outcome over total exposure, the rate per unit of exposure.

Value

A list of prior specifications including intercept, treatment, sigma (for identity links), log_sigma, slopes (named numeric scales for the session-count columns), random effects (if multilevel), and recommendations.

Details

Priors are weakly informative and expressed on the scale of the linear predictor, with prior width tied to the measurement scale. Prior width never depends on the number of observations or cases: a small sample is not information about the effect, and the data, not a narrower prior, decide how much the posterior moves.

  • Identity links: treatment and slope coefficients normal(0, 2.5 * SD), intercept student_t(3, mean, 2.5 * SD), group-level SDs half-student_t(3, 0, SD), and the residual SD half-student_t(3, 0, SDw), where SD is the outcome standard deviation and SDw the pooled within-phase SD (the outcome SD when phases are missing). Coefficients and group-level SDs scale to the outcome SD, which spans between-case differences and floor-to-ceiling effects; the residual SD prior scales to the pooled within-phase SD. The half-t form scales the SD priors to the response; brms itself uses the scale max(2.5, mad(y)), so the two differ when the outcome SD is small or the outcome is skewed. The 2.5 multiplier for coefficients carries the 2.5-unit logistic regression scale to the response scale, a package convention.

  • Logit links: treatment coefficients normal(0, 2.5), the weakly informative scale for logistic regression coefficients; intercept student_t(3, 0, 2.5) and group-level SDs half- student_t(3, 0, 2.5), as the brms defaults on non-identity links.

  • Log links: the same scale 2.5, intercept centered on the log of the outcome mean. The 2.5 scale was derived for logistic regression only; carrying it to log links is a package convention.

Shape (negative binomial, Gamma), precision (beta), and degrees-of-freedom (Student-t) parameters keep the brms defaults, for lack of an established weakly informative prior. For these families recommendations$dispersion suggests adding a second shape or precision prior to the prior sensitivity analysis.

The outcome column is outcome_var, which defaults to structure$outcome_var and then to "outcome"; with no such column the outcome-based scales fall back to 1 and 0.

The 2.5 scale presumes standardized inputs: binary inputs differing by 1 and continuous inputs scaled to SD 0.5. Level steps and condition dummies are 0/1 inputs and take the scale as is. Session-count terms (time_*, trend_*) are not standardized, so slopes holds one scale per such column, 2.5 * SD / (2 * sd(x)) on identity links and 2.5 / (2 * sd(x)) otherwise: the 2.5 scale for a coefficient on the input standardized to SD 0.5, expressed per session. assemble_brms_priors() applies them to the slope terms of a supplied formula.

log_sigma centers the intercept of a log-scale residual SD (sigma ~ phase) on the log of the pooled within-phase SD with scale 1, tying the prior to the measurement scale; the scale 1 lets the baseline SD range over a factor of about e either way and is a convention. On non-identity links the location is 0.

Examples

d <- simulate_scd_data(n_cases = 3)
structure <- list(n_levels = 2, levels = list(case = "case"))
generate_adaptive_priors(d, structure)
